questions.question: What is the primary function of a flip-flop in digital circuits?
options: To perform arithmetic operations.
To amplify analog signals.
To store a single bit of binary information.
To convert analog signals to digital.
To generate clock signals.

questions.question: In a multi-core processor system, what is the primary purpose of a cache coherence protocol (e.g., MESI)?
options: To manage virtual memory page table lookups.
To ensure that all processors have a consistent view of shared memory data.
To improve the clock frequency of individual cores.
To reduce the power consumption of the cache memory.
To convert instruction addresses to data addresses.

questions.question: In the context of hardware verification, what is the primary advantage of using FPGA-based emulation compared to software-based simulation for a large System-on-Chip (SoC) design?
options: Emulation provides exhaustive mathematical proof of correctness.
Emulation is significantly faster, allowing for more real-world test cases.
Emulation requires less setup effort and specialized hardware.
Emulation typically consumes less power during the verification process.
Emulation guarantees complete functional coverage automatically.

questions.question: Beyond simple branch prediction, what is a common technique employed in deeply pipelined processors to mitigate the performance impact of control hazards when the target of a branch instruction is known late?
options: Increasing the cache line size.
Implementing a wider Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU).
Utilizing delayed branching or branch target buffers (BTBs).
Reducing the number of pipeline stages.
Disabling instruction-level parallelism.

questions.question: Which advanced power management technique dynamically adjusts both the operating voltage and clock frequency of a processor or SoC block to optimize performance and power consumption based on workload demands?
options: Thermal throttling.
Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS).
Static timing analysis.
Register-Transfer Level (RTL) synthesis.
Test pattern generation.
